notes.text: This is a big task, so I'll work through it methodically. I'm noting that the "not patched for this event" comments should be ignored per instructions, meaning those inputs get treated normally and patched like everything else. Now I'm organizing the input list in standard order: drums first (kick, snare, hihat, toms, overheads, percussion), then bass, guitars, and keyboards.

For drums I'm ordering as Kick, Snare, HiHat, then Tom1-3 as rack toms and Tom4 as the floor tom, followed by OH L/R kept as separate mono channels, then the two percussion tracks. For bass I have DI and mic. For guitars, since EG1/EG2 and AC Guit1/AC Guit2 aren't labeled L/R, I'm keeping them as separate mono channels rather than pairing them as stereo. Same logic applies to the two keyboards - …

Now I'm listing vocals (VOX1-5), speech (HOST), and the track inputs - noting all tracks should be patched via USB per instructions rather than local sockets. I'm counting up the non-track channels needing local input sockets and hitting 29 total, but the local input bank only has 24 sockets available, so I need to figure out how the overflow gets routed to AES50-A.

I'm now assigning each channel in desk order to a socket: the first 24 non-track channels fill LCL1 through LCL24, working through kick, snare, hi-hat, toms, overheads, percussion, bass DI/mic, electric guitars, and continuing into the acoustic guitar inputs.

Beyond that, vocals 2-5 and the host mic overflow onto AES50-A ports 1-5 since local slots are exhausted, and then I'm moving on to patch the track playback channels into USB group inputs sequentially starting with track 30.

With 37 total channels confirmed within the 40-channel limit, I'm now setting up processing defaults: 40Hz high-pass for the drum category channels (kick, snare, hi-hat, toms, overheads, percussion), and 80Hz high-pass as the default for non-drum band instruments.

Refining the specific overrides: bass, keys, strings, and guitars all get 80Hz, horns get 100Hz for their thicker fundamentals, vocals and host speech both get 120Hz, and the pre-recorded tracks skip high-pass filtering entirely since they're already mixed.

For gain staging, I'm applying 20dB head-amp gain only to physically patched channels through LCL and AES50-A sockets, since USB tracks don't have a head-amp stage. Trim stays at 0dB across every channel regardless of input type. Now I'm working out the color coding scheme, assigning red to drums, blue to bass, magenta to guitars, and cyan to keyboards, with strings and brass needing their own co…

For routing, I'm establishing that all channels go to Main L/R by default, but click and guide tracks are the critical exception - per convention, these must only route to monitor busses and never touch the main mix. Other backing track channels like drums, bass, keys, and guitars tracks represent the actual band sound, so they should route to Main like any other channel.

But drum channels present a wrinkle: since they're grouped into a "Drums" mix bus that itself feeds Main, the individual drum channels should show empty main_routes since they reach Main indirectly through the bus rather than directly.
So applying this logic, Vocals channels get empty main_routes since they route through the Vocals bus, and the same applies to Keys and Horns channels through their respective busses.

Strings channels similarly route through the Strings bus with empty main_routes. Guitars and Bass have no dedicated bus, so they route directly to Main; HOST isn't excluded from main routing so it goes directly too, and drum/guide tracks route only to monitor rather than Main.
Now I'm mapping out the DCAs — Drums, Guitars, Keys, Vocals, Tracks, Strings, and Horns — each grouping their respective channels.

Since Bass isn't given its own named DCA, it falls under the "Band" catch-all category along with any other unlisted instruments. Speech DCA covers HOST, and FX DCA gathers the effects return busses like VOX Reverb, VOX Delay, Snare Verb, and INST Reverb.
Now I'm working through mute groups, starting with the Band group covering all non-vocal band instruments.

Working out the Band mute group definition: I'm interpreting it as instrumental channels only (drums, bass, guitars, keys, horns, strings), explicitly excluding vocals, speech, and tracks since the doc notes tracks aren't band instruments and get no high-pass, no Band mute, and no INST Reverb send. The Vocals mute group covers VOX1-5, Speech covers HOST, and FX covers the same effects busses.

Now I'm laying out the bus ordering: monitor busses (MON1-4) come first, then mix busses (Drums, Drums Comp, Vocals, Keys, Horns, Strings), then the FX busses. For the monitor busses specifically, I'm noting they're mono, patched to local XLR outputs 1-4, faders pulled all the way down with no main route, and every channel sends to them.

Every channel except speech (HOST) sends to each monitor bus pre-fader at -144 level unmuted, including tracks and especially click/guide since those are monitor-only sources. Moving to the mix busses, I'm defining Drums as a stereo bus with the full drum kit and percussion channels feeding the main post-fader at unity, and noting Drums Comp duplicates that same membership as a parallel compressi…

Drums Comp feeds main post-fader but with its own fader at -6dB, while its channel sends mirror the Drums bus at unity post-fader — I'm jotting compressor settings for later. Then I'm setting up Vocals (VOX1-5, excluding HOST since that's speech not vocals) and Keys (Keys1, Keys2), both stereo busses feeding main post-fader at unity with unity post-fader sends.

Now I'm working through the remaining busses: Horns (Horns1,2), Strings (Strings1,2), and the FX sends — VOX Reverb and VOX Delay both pull from all vocal channels at unity post-fader, Snare Verb takes only the snare channel pre-fader at -10dB, and INST Reverb gathers every non-drum instrument channel (bass, guitars, keys, horns, strings) — all feeding the main bus at unity post-fader.

For the Main bus itself, it's the complete mix with no direct physical output, instead routing into Matrix1, which is patched to internal XLR outputs 7 and 8. I'm structuring the outputs array to reflect Main as a non-physical routing point feeding Matrix1.

Actually, since the conventions explicitly state Main has no physical output—only feeding Matrix 1—I'll set patch to null with a note clarifying this intentional absence rather than treating it as unstated silence. Then for Matrix 1, I record kind matrix, fed by main index 1, with patch group LCL on sockets 7 and 8 as explicitly stated.

For mono status, I'll mark it false since stereo main feeding a pair of sockets implies stereo matrix, though I should flag this as inferred rather than explicit. Now I'm ready to assemble the JSON output, keeping it compact but including provenance tags, and I need to apply the head-amp gain rule—20dB gain and 0dB trim on channels with head-amp sockets like LCL and AES-A—since nothing in the sho…

For trim, I'll apply 0.0 dB universally across all channels including USB tracks, but restrict the 20dB gain to non-USB channels with actual head-amp hardware. Faders get set to -144.0 dB as instructed to leave them fully down, and since mute status isn't explicitly stated I'll leave that field null rather than assume anything. Now I'm assembling the full channel list with all these decided attri…

Next I'm defining category-to-color mappings for the mixer's visual scheme, then building the complete channels array with each entry's input source, patch assignment, processing chain, DCA routing, and mute group, following a patch group logic that fills local inputs first, then AES50-A for overflow, then USB for tracks.

So channels 1-24 get group LCL, channels 25-29 get group A for AES50-A, and tracks 30-37 get group USB, letting the code assign socket numbers within each group. Now I'm working out main_routes: Drums members route to empty since they go through the Drums bus, while Bass, Guitars, and Keys route through index 1.

Continuing through Horns, Strings, and Vocals with empty main_routes since they go through their own buses, while HOST and non-click/guide tracks route to index 1, and Click/Guide tracks stay empty since they're monitor-only. Then I'm assigning DCA groups per channel type—Drums, Band for Bass, Guitars, Keys, Horns, Strings, Vocals, and Speech for HOST—working through the track channels next.

Now I'm setting mute groups (Band for instrument channels, Vocals and Speech separately, none for Tracks), HPF values by channel type (40Hz drums, 80Hz for bass/guitars/keys/strings, 100Hz horns, 120Hz vocals/HOST, none for tracks), gain/trim settings distinguishing LCL/A channels from USB tracks, and confirming no stereo pairing since all channels remain mono including the OH L/R pair.
Now I'm working through bus sends, starting with MON1-4 which receive from every channel except HOST since speech should be excluded from monitor mixes.
I'm enumerating all 36 channel names across drums, bass, guitars, keys, horns, strings, vocals, and talkback tracks to build the explicit exclusion list for HOST.
Now I'm working through the mix bus sends: setting drum, drum comp, vocal, keys, and horns buses to post-fader unity sends, matching each bus to its corresponding source channels.

Then I'm mapping FX bus sends: VOX reverb and delay pull from all five vocal channels post-unity, snare verb takes a pre-fader -10 send from snare alone, and instrument reverb pulls from all instrument channels but sits at -144 (fully down) post-fader.

I'm setting bus destinations and fader levels too - mix and FX buses route to Main1 at unity, monitor buses go to dedicated LCL outputs with faders pulled to -144, mix bus faders stay at unity except Drums Comp at -6.0, and FX bus faders remain at unity. Now I'm building out the FX DCA group membership.

I'm checking that the FX mute group also includes the FX buses, then verifying every DCA and mute group in the array has at least one member assigned - Drums, Guitars, Keys, Vocals, Tracks, Strings, Horns, Band, Speech, FX all check out, as do the four mute groups. I'm also auditing for conflicts between conventions and explicit instructions, confirming there aren't any since the instructions dir…

Since there are no unassigned inputs or conflicts to flag, I'm now moving on to compiling notes about the compressor settings, the Main output's lack of physical patch, and the Matrix1 feed, before starting to assemble the final compact JSON output.
Writing config JSON...
I also need to capture the DCA, mute group, and main route provenance quotes from their respective category rules. Now I have everything needed to assemble the full JSON output.

I need to place the "Pads" channel, ignoring its "not patched" note since that's just informational. It falls under drums category but isn't strictly percussion, so I'm figuring out whether it goes after the overheads or alongside PERC1/PERC2 in the ordering.

Now I'm recounting the LCL patch bay to check for overflow: with Pads added, the drum count grows to 12, pushing total channel count to 24 slots by Strings2, which means VOX1 now becomes the 25th channel and overflows onto AES-A instead of fitting on LCL as before.

Since the patch system just assigns a group like "LCL" and the code auto-computes the next free socket, I don't need to manually renumber sockets — I just need to insert Pads in the right position and change VOX1's group from LCL to AES-A since LCL is now full, shifting VOX2-5 and HOST forward on AES-A accordingly.

I'll shift VOX1 to group A and update its provenance, then add a Pads channel to LCL with drums category, DCA Drums, mute group Band, and full processing chain. I also need to add Pads to the MON1-4 sends, Drums bus sends, and Drums Comp bus sends before assembling the final corrected JSON.

I'm verifying the routing and level conventions look correct, but I notice trim_db is null for USB tracks, which seems to conflict with the domain knowledge stating trim applies to every channel—I need to flag that discrepancy.
Then I confirm the channels marked "not patched for this event" are still included in the plan as instructed, so there's no omission there.

The DCA "FX" assignment looks right, correctly grouping the reverb/delay returns per convention, and the FX mute group is properly applied to those busses. But I catch a real issue: the mono field for Drums Comp and other mix busses (Drums, Vocals, Keys, Horns, Strings) plus the FX busses is marked "inferred" when the show instructions explicitly state under the Mix Busses heading that these are …

By contrast, MON1-4 correctly avoids the "inferred" tag since mono is directly stated for those busses, showing the plan is inconsistent in how it applies that label. I also verify the Snare bus send only feeds Snare Verb, that HOST bus_sends is empty as expected since speech is excluded from monitor sends, and now I'm looking at the DCA assignment for BassDI.

Checking channel ordering: with Tom1-4 present, Tom4 should be treated as the floor tom per convention, and the plan's sequence of Tom1,2,3,4,OH L,OH R,Pads,PERC1,PERC2 matches that expectation correctly.

For BassDI, gain_db of 20 seems plausible since a DI box still uses a head-amp on the local input, so it's not an omission. Now I'm cross-checking that all 38 input rows in the csv map to the 38 channel entries to confirm unassigned_inputs is properly empty.

Moving on, I'm verifying the conventions section: the FX mute group and Speech DCA are both used, and BassDI/BassMic's blue color matches house convention with no conflicts apparent. I'm also confirming the patch group math—drums, bass, guitars, keys, horns, and strings sum exactly to 24 LCL sockets, meaning VOs correctly start on AES50-A—and checking the Guitars DCA assignments for EG1, EG2, and…

Now I'm checking that the Band mute group correctly excludes tracks while including guitars, keys, horns, strings, and bass channels, and verifying vocals bus sends correctly include Vocals bus, VOX Reverb, and VOX Delay while excluding INST Reverb since vocals aren't instruments. I'm also confirming that instrument channels like guitars, keys, horns, strings, and bass all correctly include the I…

Drums correctly lack the INST Reverb send per the "but not drums" exclusion, and Snare Verb correctly appears only on Snare. Phantom power settings match the input list for OH L and Kick. I'm now flagging that trim_db is left null for USB track channels, which seems to violate the stated convention that trim applies to every channel and should default to 0dB unless overridden — this looks like a …

Checking T VOX/FX, it's correctly routed to Main since it's categorized as a track rather than click/guide. The multiple keyboards, horns, and strings channels correctly triggered creation of their respective mix busses without index conflicts. Now I'm confirming the bus ordering follows the required sequence: monitor busses first, then mix busses.

I still need to flag the trim_db null issue and the mono flag inference for explicitly stated stereo busses. DCA order (Drums, Guitars, Keys, Vocals, Tracks, Strings, Horns, Band, Speech, FX) matches convention, gain/trim values look fine, and Main 1 patch being null makes sense since it has no physical output. Matrix1 patch sockets match instructions too, and I'm now checking that Drums Comp sen…

The Drums bus sends are unity post-fader, matching the plan's 0.0 dB level with no override needed. Compressor settings aren't part of the bus object format, so the plan noting that separately is acceptable. Checking fader values, all channels are correctly set to -144 dB (fully down) per convention, bus faders like MON are also correctly at -144, and the "Beta 91A" kick mic model matches the giv…

Mix bus faders like FX are correctly at unity 0.0 dB, and MON's mono field being true matches the stated input directly without inference issues. For the findings list, I'm settling on two or three items, possibly including something about DCA/mute handling, and I'm confirming that Keys1/2 channels correctly have empty main_routes since they route through the Keys bus only, consistent with the Dr…

I'm settling on two findings total, both tied to intent-severity, and gathering the exact convention quotes to support them: one about trim being set to 0dB unless overridden, and one confirming mix busses and FX busses are defined as stereo. Now I'm ready to write up the findings.
